role: AUTHOR primary-document analysis, not an independent review

primaryStudies.title: Kinetic of Esterification of Ethyl Alcohol by Acetic Acid on a Catalytic Resin
primaryStudies.author: Erol İnce
primaryStudies.publication: Pamukkale University Journal of Engineering Sciences 2002, 8(1), 109–113
primaryStudies.actualExperimentalSystem: Ethanoic acid + ethanol ⇌ ethyl ethanoate + water; resin-catalysed stirred batch under reflux at controlled temperature.
primaryStudies.commonSample: Section2.1/2.2, PDFp2: successive approximately500µL liquid aliquots from one reaction vessel; each aliquot analysed for all four components by one GC system. No combining separate starting vessels.
primaryStudies.method: HP6890 GC, serial TCD/FID, HP-Innowax column; TCD quantitative processing, FID reference/mass-balance support.
primaryStudies.publishedActualObservations: PDFp3 Figures1–4 are actual plotted conversion-time series with nonzero incomplete conversion, approaching plateaus. PDFp4–5 Table2 reports experimental equilibrium constant3.98. The table is not a list of four raw detector peaks.
documentedControls: Changed starting ratios, water amounts and catalyst loadings
notDocumented: Individual raw chromatograms, retention times and measured four-component peak areas
Species reference-standard/blank results and matrix-recovery/selectivity tests
Validated quench or preservation time for each withdrawn aliquot
Run-specific chemical-equilibrium claim independently checked against the unusual initial-water omission in equation6
primaryStudies.allowedConclusion: Authentic published reaction and analytical-method context with incomplete conversion; conditional four-species coexistence under the authors’ identity/closed-balance assumptions. Not a fully auditable four-species same-time chromatogram dossier.

actualSourceConsistencyFinding.source: PDFp4 equation6 and PDFp5 Table2 compared with PDFp2 Table1
actualSourceConsistencyFinding.observed: Equation6 uses X_Ae squared as product term although initial water is nonzero in Table1; Table2 gives k1=0.0244 and k2=0.0047, whose ratio is approximately5.19, while reporting Kexp3.98. The text says Kexp=k1/k2. These inconsistencies prevent using the reported constant as a self-validating equilibrium proof.
actualSourceConsistencyFinding.decision: HOLD numerical/model consistency, author source audit only

primaryStudies.title: Heat on – Calibration of IR Spectroscopy at Process Conditions for Continuous Esterification
primaryStudies.actualExperimentalSystem: Continuous acid/alcohol esterification in a heated meander reactor; ethanol and methanol experiments explicitly distinguished.
primaryStudies.commonSample: Section2.2/2.3, PDFp2–3: one inline ATR probe immediately after the reactor analyses the shared stream at process conditions. The later offline NMR tube is explicitly a different sampling/measurement time.
primaryStudies.method: ATR-FTIR with PLS regression using prepared pure/matrix compositions at process conditions; validation and cross-NMR discussed.
primaryStudies.publishedActualObservations: PDFp4 Figure3 is calibration, not an unknown reaction sample. PDFp5 Figure4 is conversion-based calibration, not an executed equilibrium composition. PDFp6 Figure5 is the measured methanol reaction, not the ethanol reaction. It reports positive incomplete acid conversion with residence-time dependence.
documentedControls: No-catalyst calibration with short residence time limiting unintended reaction
Offline NMR check for unexpected side products; delay prevents exact composition equivalence

measurementErrorExample.source: PDFp5 Table1, ethanol multicomponent model, RMSEP percent

notDocumented: Raw four-species spectrum and independent assignments for one named reaction point in the main article
The ethanol reaction-component plot in the supporting material, which returnedHTTP403 during this preparation
primaryStudies.allowedConclusion: Authentic process analytical controls and actual published reaction data. Continuous stationarity is not evidence of equal forward/reverse rates. Calibration mixtures, a delayed offline NMR sample and an ethanol/methanol substitution cannot be presented as one equilibrium sample.

nonTransferRule: Each study retains its own sample, method and controls. Schnoor’s calibration cannot retroactively validate İnce’s GC aliquots. No absent blank, recovery result, raw spectrum or executed learner experiment is invented.
remainingDuties: Auditable species-specific observations for one identified, composition-preserved equilibrium sample
An applicable experiment-execution operator requires genuine performance evidence; supplied published data certify interpretation only
machineM7Boundary: No human-approval requirement is added. These are concrete chemical/source evidence limits and independent machine-review duties.
